course_info.faculty: Faculty of Engineering and Natural Sciences

catalog_course_description: Aims to illustrate the basic principles of molecular and evolutionary genetics from Mendel to modern molecular biology. Examples will be chosen from prokaryotic and eukaryotic organisms and topics include: principles of heredity and variation and their application to evolution and development, phsicochemical nature of the gene, problems of recombination and gene action, selection.
course_learning_outcomes: Upon successful completion of this course, students should be able to: Identify the concepts of heredity, the chemical nature of the hereditary material, and its action.
Describe the rewarding uses of genetics in their other subjects, e.g., biology, medicine.
Interpret genetic information, such as popular news reports, management decisions faced by your company, and personal health choices of you or your family.
course_objective: To teach fundamentals of traditional and modern concepts genetics.

resources: Genetics, D. Peter Snustad, Michael J. Simmons. Essential Genetics and Genomics, Daniel L. Hartl
course_materials.technology_requirements: All the students should have access to a laptop
